claims.text: Conventionally processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of about 786 MPa.
Conventionally processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of about 1314 MPa.
Conventionally processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has approximately 13.5% uniform tensile elongation.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has established impact-induced chemical-energy release.
Hot deformation followed by rapid annealing will refine the grain structure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The treatment will produce a more uniform grain structure with enhanced grain-boundary characteristics.
The enhanced grain-boundary characteristics will improve dislocation mobility.
The refined microstructure will mitigate strain localization and distribute tensile strain more uniformly.
More uniform strain distribution will delay localized failure and suppress early crack initiation.
Short-range order underpins the high yield strength of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The thermomechanical treatment will preserve the short-range order of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Preserving short-range order will maintain the alloy's impact-triggered chemical-energy release.
At room temperature and approximately 10^-3 s^-1, treatment will increase uniform tensile elongation by at least about 20–30% relative to a 13.5% baseline.
The treated alloy's yield strength will remain within ±5% of 786 MPa.
The treated alloy's impact-triggered energy release will remain comparable to that of untreated HfZrTiTa0.53.

contradictions.description: The query describes 13.5% as terminal strain in the context of reported compressive properties, whereas the hypothesis repeatedly reclassifies it as uniform tensile elongation. Terminal strain and uniform tensile elongation are distinct measurements.
